title: Shapechanging
summary: Life magick that reshapes the caster or another creature.

claims.text: Reworking one's own body takes Life 3 for slight shifts, Life 4 for a whole new shape and Life 5 for a flawless change; working on another living being needs one Rank above that.
Taking a similar form yourself needs two successes and a very unlike form three; turning someone else needs four for a near shape and five or more for a wholly alien one.
A botched Life transformation leaves horrible mutations, and the Storyteller may let even a failed roll leave hidden flaws that show up later.

title: Psychic and spiritual elementalism
summary: Commanding matter and flame through will and the Spheres.

claims.text: Lifting or steering objects with Forces asks for steady concentration and a Willpower roll on top of the Arete roll.
How vulgar a levitation is depends on the size of the thing, how openly it is done and whether some believable device seems to explain it.
Controlling flames that already burn uses Mind 3 with Forces 2, and the Storyteller may charge a Willpower point for big or unlikely fires.
Traditional elementalists treat the elements as living things that can be called up as entities.

title: Quintessence through sacrifice
summary: Drawing raw magickal energy out of living offerings.

claims.text: Prime 3 lets a mage tear Quintessence from the Pattern of an unwilling living creature, an act that draws grim consequences.
A creature of human size holds about 10 points, a small animal three to five, and a very large beast 15 or more.
Whoever takes in Quintessence from a living sacrifice also takes on the Resonance of the deed.
Prime 4 can disintegrate an object given as an offering and Prime 5 a living being; this scatters the energy back into Creation instead of feeding the caster.

title: Necrosynthesis
summary: A blatant death-magick that rots living flesh.

claims.text: Entropy 4 joined with Life 3 sends necrotic decay through a body for aggravated damage; adding Prime 2 can breed maggots inside the victim.
A caster who uses it gains a dot of Jhor or Entropic Synergy Resonance and is likely to suffer a Morbidity Quiet at the next Paradox.

title: Lichedom
summary: A whispered rite of undying for necromancers.

claims.text: Mystic gossip tells of a damned working that leaves a necromancer in a state of living death.
The lore is said to come from old Egyptian and Roman rites, later polished by rogue Hermetic practice, and to yield a thing that is at once mage, mortal, corpse and spirit and yet none of them.

title: Spirit possession
summary: Hosting, resisting and using a possessing spirit.

claims.text: Sleepers with Willpower 5 or less cannot throw out a possessing spirit and must wait for it to leave or be exorcised.
Mages, other Night-Folk and strong-willed people can fight back with an extended, resisted Willpower roll to 10 successes, each side rolling against the other's Willpower.
The host usually gets one try per day, with an extra chance when the spirit forces something truly unbearable.
A mage can also use a bond with a possessing totem as the focus of an Effect, such as growing fangs through Wolf.
